affected_parts.evidence: Mature leaves develop longitudinal stripes or streaks... Infected canes are stunted with short internodes giving them a bushy appearance... The vascular bundles are deep red.

summary.value: Gummosis causes longitudinal stripes on mature leaves that are initially pale yellow and later turn brown, with affected tissues slowly drying up. Infected canes become stunted with short internodes and a bushy appearance, producing a dull yellow bacterial ooze when cut.
summary.evidence: Mature leaves develop longitudinal stripes or streaks that are 3-7 mm in width and several centimeters in length. The stripes appear around the affected veins and near the tip. Initially the stripes are pale yellow in color and later turn brown. The affected tissues slowly dry up. Infected canes are stunted with short internodes giving them a bushy appearance. When stunted canes are cut, a dull yellow bacterial ooze (gum) comes out from the cut ends.

diagnostic_features.value: Distinctive dull yellow bacterial ooze from cut canes, deep red vascular bundles, specific stripe width of 3-7 mm, and bushy appearance from short internodes
diagnostic_features.evidence: When stunted canes are cut, a dull yellow bacterial ooze (gum) comes out from the cut ends. The vascular bundles are deep red.

extractions.source_title: Sugarcane Mosaic Disease: Characteristics, Identification and Control

disease_name.evidence: Mosaic is one of the most important sugarcane diseases, caused by single or compound infection of Sugarcane mosaic virus (SCMV), Sorghum mosaic virus (SrMV), and/or Sugarcane streak mosaic virus (SCSMV).

type_of_disease.evidence: Mosaic is one of the main viral sugarcane diseases.

affected_parts.evidence: In infected sugarcane plants, chlorophyll is destroyed, photosynthesis is weakened, and growth is significantly inhibited, resulting in shorter internodes, fewer mill-able stems, shorter roots. Systemic infection is caused by the virus after it invades sugarcane. They move quickly in vascular bundles, along with the flow of plant nutrients. As a result, the virus can spread to almost every tissue, even the whole stool.

summary.value: Leaves exhibit irregular yellow and green mosaic patterns (inlays, stripes, and mottles) alternating with parallel veins, clearly visible against sunlight. Severely infected leaves turn yellow or yellow-white with red punctate necrosis or abnormally twisted tips.
summary.evidence: In comparison to healthy leaves, there are many irregular yellow and green inlays, stripes, or mottles alternate with parallel veins on symptomatic leaves, more clearly visible against the sunlight. Some show very obvious whole leaf chlorosis, and the seriously infected leaves turn yellow or yellow white, leaving only a few green islets or a small amount of red punctate necrosis, or the tips of new leaves are abnormally twisted.

diagnostic_features.value: Yellow and green mosaic pattern (inlays, stripes, and mottles) alternating with parallel veins on symptomatic leaves, distinctly visible against sunlight.
diagnostic_features.evidence: there are many irregular yellow and green inlays, stripes, or mottles alternate with parallel veins on symptomatic leaves, more clearly visible against the sunlight.
